purpose: Owner correction: broad maze-building battlefield; initial image is open field and a later edit will show player-built alternating tower barriers
maze_example_prompt:
Edit this exact D1 OPEN BUILDING FIELD image into a before/after companion called "D2 — PLAYER-BUILT MAZE".
Preserve the EXACT outer gray-field boundary, its generous width, paving scale, camera, landscape, portal at upper right, soul objective at lower left, and every resource cluster. Do not reshape the terrain into a zigzag. The maze must be created ONLY BY PLAYER-PLACED TOWERS inside this same wide gray battlefield.
Add exactly TWO substantial staggered transverse rows of the existing small red-roof wooden Rapid watchtowers, with one or two existing stone-enclosed spoon catapults integrated or nearby. Each defense occupies one construction cell; the tower rows block their occupied cells. Keep them at the same scale as the existing reference towers, never inflate their size. Towers in each barrier touch through adjacent occupied footprints; avoid small accidental traversable holes within a row. These are clearly repeated towers, not a new wall unit, fence, terrain obstacle or continuous brick wall.
The first barrier nearer the red portal is anchored at ONE gray/green side boundary and extends across approximately three quarters of the gray area's width; it stops with a clearly visible 3-cell-wide OPEN PASSAGE at the other gray/green side. The second barrier farther toward the soul objective is anchored at the OPPOSITE side and extends across three quarters, leaving its 3-cell-wide OPEN PASSAGE on the opposite side from the first. Keep at least 4-5 free construction cells of longitudinal space between the two rows. At the bend the field remains wide enough for these rows and passageways. No full closure, no ring around the objective, no fenced-in pocket, no extra maze branches, no towers on grass, no independent decorative walls blocking a path.
Thus the one valid enemy flow is: leave red portal -> cross toward the opening around the FREE TIP of barrier 1 -> traverse across the wide space BETWEEN the two barriers -> go around the opposite FREE TIP of barrier 2 -> continue to the blue objective. This makes a broad PLAYER-BUILT ZIGZAG inside the otherwise gently curved open field. All parts of this walkable route remain connected and gray. No path goes across grass, through a tower footprint, over a tower, or through a sealed wall.
To make the design readable, add a thin translucent warm-gold route line with a few small arrowheads through the actual OPEN CELL PASSAGES just described. This line is a concept-only explanatory overlay, not a runtime rail/road. Redistribute the same small cartoon skeletons along the line, including at both free tower-row ends. Route line must visibly go around the tower barriers, staying a clear distance from their bases. Empty paving remains visible between rows and around the approach.
Same game cartoon art, no new gameplay content, no changes to attack values/economy or land scale. Do not add HUD, minimap, numbers, labels, arrows outside the route overlay, or text except replacing the upper-left title with exactly "D2 — PLAYER-BUILT MAZE".
maze_refinement_prompt:
Make ONE precise topology correction to this D2 PLAYER-BUILT MAZE illustration. Preserve the entire image, wide gray-field outline, camera, art, landmark positions, golden route overlay and the two existing tower-row orientations.
The desired golden route goes around the LEFT free tip of the UPPER barrier, then around the RIGHT free tip of the LOWER barrier. Those two openings must remain wide and fully open.
Close ONLY the unintended opposite-side bypasses:
1. At the RIGHT end of the UPPER barrier, extend the row with the minimum few additional adjacent existing Rapid towers until the final occupied cell meets the RIGHT gray/grass boundary. There must be no spare gray walking strip around this anchored end.
2. At the LEFT end of the LOWER barrier, extend the row with the minimum few additional adjacent existing Rapid towers until the final occupied cell meets the LEFT gray/grass boundary. There must be no spare gray walking strip around this anchored end.
Keep every tower base inside the gray construction field, and let each anchored row meet its boundary with no footpath between its last occupied base and the grass. Do not put towers outside on green terrain, do not add walls, fences, rocks or new obstacle types, and do not reshape the gray field. The player creates these barriers only by occupying cells with the familiar tower.
Do NOT close the intentional upper-left or lower-right OPEN tips or the connected channel between rows. Do NOT put a tower on the golden route. Exactly one open end per barrier, alternating sides, with a connected portal-to-objective route through both openings. The small number of end-extension towers must match existing size/perspective; no enlargement or giant terminal towers.
Keep the exact title D2 — PLAYER-BUILT MAZE. Everything else is unchanged.
width_status: Agent starting hypothesis for visual study, not accepted tuning or pixel-measured geometry
open_field_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a NEW revised level-layout concept for Not 3A Game, correcting an important design misunderstanding in the earlier route illustration.
Reference image 1: actual game visual identities and scale. Reference image 2: the earlier A layout, useful ONLY for cartoon art language; its narrow pre-bent road is the problem to correct. Do NOT preserve its narrow route topology.
Core game: mazing tower defense. Towers themselves are obstacles; the PLAYER lays alternating rows of towers to create the long zigzag enemy route. Terrain must provide a generously WIDE BUILDING FIELD. The gray area is a spacious construction battlefield with a large gentle overall bend, not a narrow pre-authored serpentine track.
Show a single wide landscape elevated orthographic tactical overview in the same smooth outlined hand-painted fantasy cartoon style: worn gray paving with grassy joints, yellow-green meadow/earth patches, small pale boulders, conifers, dark rusty ore, sparse shrubs/flowers and low broken roadside masonry. Continuous larger green world beyond every frame edge, no horizon, map border, cliffs or floating island.
One intact dark slate RED VORTEX PORTAL near the upper-right end, one BLUE SOUL SPHERE beneath an ice dome on a slate bowl/base near the lower-left end. Preserve the current game's specific recognizable portal/objective. Each landmark has a roughly 3-by-3 construction-cell footprint. They must remain separated, with a substantial open gray battlefield BETWEEN them.
Make the gray shape an elongated broad construction tract with ONE spacious, gentle elbow or very relaxed arc. Its usable width stays approximately TWELVE TO SIXTEEN ONE-TOWER BUILDING CELLS across, including at the bend. Keep an approximately 17.2-cell straight-line portal-to-objective separation as an initial design study, derived from doubling the current 8.6-cell test distance. Width and enemy travel are separate design quantities. The broad field may allow a fairly direct route before the player builds; that is intentional. Do not force a zigzag merely through narrow paving. Do not create multiple narrow arms or green wedges cutting almost across the gray area. At the bend the field should remain a generous rounded elbow, not a bottleneck.
Use the paving and restrained thin construction-cell guides to make the scale understandable: one tower occupies ONE grid cell; landmarks occupy 3x3; show at least twelve empty tower-sized spaces across a representative width. This is a scale/composition study, not a pixel-exact measured plan. Gray band occupies much of the middle composition but green land still surrounds it. Maintain the current fixed steep elevated orthographic camera, legible feet and clear building space.
This is the OPEN FIELD version: place only TWO small reference defenses at gray-field outer margins, one red-roof timber Rapid watchtower and one stone-enclosed wooden spoon catapult. They must be the familiar project towers, at the SAME CELL SCALE. Leave almost all the gray battlefield empty, especially its middle. A few small cartoon skeletons may indicate the initial direct route, but no authored lane, arrows or drawn maze. No factories, new buildings, wall-unit type or new enemy role.
Title only: "D1 — OPEN BUILDING FIELD" unobtrusively at upper left. No other labels, HUD, minimap, legend, dimension numbers or branding. Prioritize the visual message: MANY rows of towers could fit here; the overall terrain bends gently because the wide construction field, not a slender path, determines the geometry.
